grain_rationale: The profile shows row_count=166158 and duplicate_row_rate=0.0, meaning every row is a distinct flight record with no exact duplicate rows to absorb. Each row is one flight event (a scheduled flight on a given date, from a given NYC origin, with a given carrier and flight number), so grain_type is transaction. No single column is unique on its own (origin_airport distinct_count 3, carrier_code 16, flight_number 2994, flight_date 181), so a derived identity flight_identity over (flight_date, carrier_code, flight_number, origin_airport) is used; the zero duplicate_row_rate confirms this tuple needs no further deduplication logic.

fields.name: flight_date
fields.description: Calendar date of the scheduled flight, ranging 2013-01-01 to 2013-06-30 per the profile's min/max, with null_rate 0.0 making it always present as a dimension date attribute.

fields.name: carrier_code
fields.description: Two-letter carrier code (e.g. 9E, AA, DL) with 16 distinct values and null_rate 0.0, used as the airline dimension lookup key.

fields.name: flight_number
fields.description: Operating flight number, integer ranging 1 to 8500 with 2994 distinct values and null_rate 0.0; it labels the specific flight rather than measuring a quantity, so it is a dimension.

fields.name: origin_airport
fields.description: Three-letter origin airport code, one of EWR, JFK, LGA (distinct_count 3) with null_rate 0.0, identifying the NYC origin dimension.

fields.name: sched_dep_hhmm
fields.description: Scheduled departure time encoded as HHMM integer, ranging 500 to 2359 with null_rate 0.0; it labels a time-of-day rather than measuring a quantity, so it is a dimension.

fields.name: dest_airport
fields.description: Three-letter destination airport code, one of 100 distinct values with null_rate 0.0, identifying the destination dimension.

fields.name: tail_number
fields.description: Aircraft tail number, 3825 distinct values with null_rate 0.009154 (1521 nulls); nullable because some flight records lack a registered tail number.

fields.name: is_cancelled

fields.name: dep_hhmm
fields.description: Actual departure time encoded as HHMM integer, ranging 1 to 2400 with null_rate 0.029388 (4883 nulls); nullable because a flight that never departed keeps no actual departure time per the operator context.

fields.name: dep_delay_minutes
fields.description: Departure delay in minutes, ranging -33 (early) to 1301 with null_rate 0.029388 matching flights that never departed; a measure aggregated across flights.

fields.name: arr_hhmm
fields.description: Actual arrival time encoded as HHMM integer, ranging 1 to 2400 with null_rate 0.0307 (5101 nulls) for flights without an actual arrival; a dimension time label.

fields.name: sched_arr_hhmm
fields.description: Scheduled arrival time encoded as HHMM integer, ranging 1 to 2359 with null_rate 0.0, a dimension time label always present.

fields.name: arr_delay_minutes
fields.description: Arrival delay in minutes, ranging -86 to 1272 with null_rate 0.032981 (5480 nulls) for flights lacking an actual arrival; a measure aggregated across flights.

fields.name: air_time_minutes
fields.description: Actual air time in minutes, ranging 20 to 695 with null_rate 0.032981 matching flights without actual times; a measure of flight duration.

fields.name: distance_miles
fields.description: Great-circle distance flown in miles, ranging 80 to 4984 with null_rate 0.0; a measure summed or averaged across flights.

fields.name: sched_dep_hour_local
fields.description: Scheduled departure hour in local time, integer 5-23 (19 distinct values) with null_rate 0.0; a dimension time-of-day bucket.

fields.name: sched_dep_minute_local
fields.description: Scheduled departure minute in local time, integer 0-59 with null_rate 0.0; a dimension time-of-day detail.

fields.name: departure_hour_utc
fields.description: Scheduled departure timestamp in UTC, truncated to the hour per the sample values (each sample advances by exactly one hour, e.g. 2013-01-01T10:00:00 through 2013-01-01T19:00:00), ranging 2013-01-01T10:00:00 to 2013-07-01T03:00:00 with null_rate 0.0; chosen as the event time column at hour grain.

fields.name: carrier_name

fields.name: aircraft_manufacture_year

fields.name: aircraft_seat_count

fields.name: aircraft_engine_type
fields.description: Aircraft engine type (e.g. Turbo-fan, Turbo-jet) with 6 distinct values and null_rate 0.160426 matching the aircraft join floor; a dimension label.

fields.description: Destination airport's longest runway in feet, ranging 5076 to 16000 with null_rate 0.02089 matching the destination join floor; a static airport attribute, so it is a dimension.

fields.name: captured_at
fields.description: Ingestion capture timestamp recorded by the pipeline, with only 16 distinct values clustered around 2026-09-02T23:25:51 through 2026-09-02T23:26:06 and null_rate 0.0; it marks when the row was captured, not the flight event, so it is a dimension rather than the time field.

category_description: Each row of flight_segments represents one scheduled flight segment: a specific carrier's flight number departing from a NYC-area origin (JFK, LGA, or EWR) on a given date, carrying its scheduled and actual departure/arrival times, delays, distance, and the joined carrier, aircraft registry, and airport attributes.
purpose: This mapping declares how the silver.silver_flights table enters the gold unified event star as the flight_segments category, naming its event time column, grain, identity, and field roles for the deterministic modeling engine that renders the gold fact and dimension models from it.
usage: The modeling engine consumes this mapping to emit the gold flight_segments fact at hour grain on departure_hour_utc, keyed by the derived flight_identity tuple of flight_date, carrier_code, flight_number, and origin_airport; the rendered ODCS mapping contract is then gated by a validator and `datacontract lint`, and a human reviews and edits the draft before approval.
limitations: This mapping does not filter cancelled flights (is_cancelled) or flights with no actual departure/arrival times, which per the operator context keep their scheduled times and no actual ones; it also does not resolve the aircraft and destination join gaps shown by their non-zero null_rate (0.160426 for aircraft fields and 0.02089 for destination fields), leaving any exclusion, backfill, or completeness decisions to downstream consumers.
